full_instruction: Write a short story about a scientist who starts seeing other versions of her own life, from parallel worlds. She feels a need to write everything down, even things that don't make sense yet. Write the story as scattered notebook entries, out of order. Include the word “adjacent” somewhere. Somewhere in the story, show that she isn't just seeing other timelines — she is slowly blending into them, and by the end she won't be able to tell which life was really hers. End the story with a notebook entry in handwriting she doesn't recognize as her own.

text:
### Notebook Entry 1

**The Paradox of Perception**

Just found out I can see other worlds... Ours. It's terrifying, fascinating. Each time it happens, there are two versions of me at once—just adjacent to each other, watching the same world unfold differently.

### Notebook Entry 2

**Reality Shifts**

I've been keeping track of these changes: slight differences in behavior of my peers, minor architectural variations in my house, even small alterations in historical events. It's as if I'm peering through a kaleidoscope that never stops shifting.

### Notebook Entry 3

**The Unnamed Voice**

There's something whispering to me from the edges of these other worlds—a voice so familiar yet strangely foreign—telling me things about myself that only another version could know. It makes sense now, why I've always felt like someone else was looking back at me in the mirror.

### Notebook Entry 4

**Crossed Realms**

I tried to reach out once... no, it vanished as quickly as it appeared—a fleeting glimpse into a life not lived but for a moment seen through my eyes. It left behind an echo of questions I can't shake off: Who is this alternate me? What did they choose?

### Notebook Entry 5

**Fragmented Memories**

Some memories feel too vivid to be just dreams. Places, people... They're right there, adjacent to the life I'm living now but not quite part of it. It's disorienting yet strangely comforting knowing someone else lived those moments.

### Notebook Entry 6

**The Unraveling Threads**

I've started writing everything down—these glimpses into other lives—to make sense of them somehow. But every entry feels like a drop in the ocean, trying to capture an endless sea of possibilities that are just beyond my reach.

### Notebook Entry 7

**A New Perspective**

It's strange how one moment can change your entire perception of time and space. I've gone from feeling alone in this experience to realizing there might be others out there, living parallel lives, seeing me as clearly as I see them now.

### Notebook Entry 8

**The Edge of Knowing**

Every day brings new clues but also more questions. The lines between worlds blur—sometimes merging into one another without warning. And with each blending, I feel a part of my identity slipping away...

### Notebook Entry 9

**Blurred Lines**

I'm starting to blend into the other lives I see. It's like watching yourself from afar; you notice differences in choices and paths taken but can't quite grasp why those differences exist until they become indistinguishable.

### Notebook Entry 10

**A Stranger Writes Back**

Someone wrote in my notebook today—an alien script, unfamiliar yet eerily familiar. Whoever they are, it feels like we're connected by something beyond our current understanding of reality. It's both exhilarating and terrifying to think I might not be alone after all.

### Notebook Entry 11

**The Last Page**

I don't recognize the handwriting anymore. The words flow differently now—a foreign dance across the page that speaks volumes without needing translation. Perhaps this is how it ends: intertwined with another life so completely there's no clear beginning or end to either existence.

full_instruction: Write a short story about the last crew member left alive on a broken-down ship, recording one final message before the air runs out. He copes with dark, deadpan jokes. Write it as one single message, with no breaks or separate scenes. Include the word “manifest,” used with two different meanings. Somewhere in the story, show that he isn't really the last one alive — the ship's cat also survived, and he's been talking to it the whole time without saying so out loud. End the message with him giving the cat a name.

text:
"Alright, let me see here... I'm probably going to be the only thing left from this ship when the oxygen runs dry. My name is Jack, and as for manifesting — no, wait, that's not right at all. Manifest as in what remains after we're gone? Yeah, that's it. The manifest of survivors: just me now.

This whole situation’s like a bad sitcom, honestly. Me and the ship cat here have been keeping each other company while everyone else was probably off living their lives or whatever. I've got to admit, though, she’s been more entertaining than most people in quarantine. We’ve named her Kitty, of course - not that you can hear me saying it out loud.

We tried making jokes about how we were the last two alive for a while. You know, because when things are grim, humor's all you got. But then again, maybe it was just me laughing at myself... I guess there really isn't any other option left here. Anyway, Kitty seems pretty okay with my dark sense of humor though — or she might just think I'm talking to myself.

So yeah, that’s the story so far. Once the air runs out… well, let's just say it won’t be long before we join the manifest ourselves. Or maybe not; perhaps there will still be some semblance of humanity left alive somewhere else? Who knows? But until then, Kitty and I have got each other.

Hey, if you're out there... Kitty might hear you someday. And hey, just remember: even in this desolate existence, we've got purrs to keep us going."

text:
I sat there at my desk, pencils poised above paper, waiting for the quiz to begin when suddenly it hit me—I tapped my pencil louder than ever before.

I stared at the chapter number on my sheet: I had been studying Chapter 3 all semester! It wasn't until this very moment that panic set in. My mind raced through equations and historical events from a completely different unit, desperate attempts to convince myself of some hidden wisdom. But as time ticked away, dread clawed its way up my throat; doom seemed inevitable.

Just then, the bell rang signaling not the start of our test but rather its postponement till next week—a fate worse than failure itself!

text:
I sat back on my chair, exhausted from hours spent poring over history textbooks for our weekly quiz tomorrow. Little did I know that today would be unlike any other at Jefferson Middle School.

As Mr. Jenkins entered the room with his slightly disheveled hair and enthusiastic grin, he announced the distribution of quizzes meant for Mrs. Thompson's class instead of ours - a disaster waiting to happen.

I quickly flipped through my textbook searching desperately for an escape route from this academic catastrophe; inspiration struck like lightning: What if I claimed the wrong quiz?

That evening after dinner and homework completion left me alone with looming doom, I grabbed notebook paper and began scribbling random facts frantically hoping it would seem plausible in class the next morning. Unbeknownst to anyone else, including myself - what I was actually studying were notes on next week's chapter!

The following day brought panic as we received our quizzes only to discover they weren't ours - doomed unless Timmy could pull off this elaborate ruse convincingly! As he scribbled answers confidently using his newly-acquired knowledge about next week's material, no one suspected their quiet classmate might just have an ace up his sleeve after all.

But fate had other plans in store because when the bell rang signaling the end of that fateful period, Mr. Jenkins informed us all: "Ladies and Gentlemen," he announced with a smirk on his face, "it seems there's been some confusion regarding today's quiz." The entire class erupted into laughter while I stood there nervously awaiting further instructions.

Mr. Jenkins continued explaining how somehow both classes accidentally received each other's quizzes by mistake - ours ended up being meant for Mrs. Thompson's science class and vice versa! Our weekly history quiz got postponed till next week anyway, leaving us all chuckling at our own mishap while Timmy grinned sheepishly knowing he'd managed to sneak past everyone undetected using knowledge meant for another chapter entirely.

And so ends the tale of young Timmy Thompson who cleverly used misplaced materials destined for someone else's studies - proving once again that sometimes being prepared can pay off even when you're caught up in academic chaos!

text:
As Timmy stepped up to the projector, clutching his slides, he couldn't help but feel a flutter of nerves. "Let's see here... Slide One: 'Introduction to Python.' Perfect," he thought to himself as the first slide flickered into view.

The audience leaned in, intrigued by his neatly organized presentation on creating a simple game using Python. But then, without warning, another tab opened mid-presentation—clearly not part of his slides. "Oh no!" Timmy muttered under his breath, watching in horror as the projector displayed his browser history instead.

"Slide Two: 'Debugging 101.' This is going to be awkward," he whispered, trying to regain control. The class erupted into silence, save for the occasional gasp and chuckle from Timmy's classmates as they realized what had happened.

"But wait!" a voice called out from the back row. "Those are just tutorials on fixing bugs! Like the one I'm presenting about!" Timmy blurted, his face turning bright red as he pointed to the screen. The teacher looked over, her calm demeanor momentarily shattered by the chaos unfolding before her.

"Timmy," she said, voice steady and reassuring despite the uproar, "this is quite a unique approach to demonstrating your project." Slowly but surely, heads nodded in agreement, and applause began to fill the room as Timmy realized that his accidental display had inadvertently proven just how much work he'd put into solving the very bug he was discussing.

text: Pixel stood before his class ready to present Governor Carrot Top's veggie democracy, but instead of slides filled with vibrant visuals about carrot-themed governance, an unexpected twist awaited as his browser history took center stage. To the astonishment of all present in room 207 at Lincoln Middle School, images from searches like "Best pizza recipes" and particularly embarrassing moments like pet hamster bathroom breaks were displayed on the screen behind him—images that's not supposed to be there. Mrs. Thompson, ever composed amidst chaos, calmly approached to guide Pixel through troubleshooting their technological hiccup. With a mix of embarrassment and newfound notoriety among classmates, Pixel promised improvements for next time, learning that even unexpected detours can lead to valuable lessons in both coding and internet safety. Unbeknownst to his classmates or teacher yet glaringly obvious on the screen behind him was forty open tutorials on how precisely fix the exact bug he'd been discussing—each one a testament to hours spent debugging after school when no one was watching except for Pixel's curious mind. Laughter echoed throughout the room as Mrs. Thompson quipped about installing an ad-blocker, turning what could have been mortifying into a shared moment of amusement within their community at Lincoln Middle School. In that momentary embarrassment turned collective awe, the class erupted in applause not just at his mishap but recognizing through those forty tutorials—the dedication behind every line of code and the perseverance to overcome challenges head-on—proof positive of Pixel's commitment to learning and growth despite any technological detours along the way.

text: Billy stood nervously behind the podium, clutching the tattered notes he had clung to for dear life. With a deep breath, he began his speech: "As your class president, I pledge to bring more recess and pizza parties..." Halfway through, he realized he'd forgotten every single card and started freestyling with wild enthusiasm. "We need better Wi-Fi!" he declared suddenly. The entire audience erupted into applause. Billy's spontaneous ideas were far superior to anything scripted; they were creative, engaging, and most importantly, unique. As the votes poured in, it became clear that his unscripted brilliance had won him the presidency. The mirror never talks back.

text:
Here is the story ending with Alex winning specifically due to his improvised ideas:

Alex Thompson sat nervously on his bed, reviewing his presidential campaign speech over and over again while looking into his own eyes in the bathroom mirror.

"You see, if we had more recess time, kids could run around and get rid of all their excess energy. That would make them happier and better focused for learning," he continued in a monotone voice, flipping through his note cards.

"Another thing our school should do is partner with local farms so students can go on field trips to pick apples in the fall or harvest pumpkins in the autumn." He glanced at the mirror as if expecting a reaction. The mirror never talks back.

"I know it sounds crazy," Alex said between breaths, running his fingers through messy hair. "But I'm sure if we just give recess a chance and organize these farm visits, our school will be transformed!"

He snapped shut the mirror's lid, feeling deflated but determined to practice one more time before heading downstairs for the big day.

Alex gathered up crumpled pieces of paper covered in scrawled notes - "Promote more recess!", "Organize fun field trips!" and headed out without looking back, hoping that maybe all those mirror rehearsals had done some good after all. 

As he stood on the podium in front of the student body gathered for debates, Alex cleared his throat again.

"Well," he began between shaky breaths, "you see, if we had more recess breaks throughout the day, like 20 minutes each, kids could run around and get rid of all their excess energy! That would make them happier and better focused for learning!"

"Another thing we should do is partner with local farms so students can pick apples in the fall or harvest pumpkins in the autumn!" His freestyle ideas were somehow even more compelling than his prepared notes. Laughter erupted from the crowd.

"I know it sounds crazy," Alex said between breaths, running his fingers through hair. "But I'm sure if we just give recess a chance and organize these farm visits, our school will be transformed!"

He took one last look at the remaining cards strewn on the podium floor before folding them up hastily and shoving them into his pocket.

"Any questions?" he asked, barely registering the sounds of stunned silence in response. 

A few nervous giggles broke out as Alex shuffled towards his desk to wait for the results - whatever they may be. He had a feeling this was going to be one memorable term.

THE END
